newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani vegoil rates seen firm next week.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani vegoil rates seen firm next week.

text.p: Pakistani vegetable oil rates will remain firm in the next trading week on an increased demand in the local market because of the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan, dealers said.
They said the consumption of vegoil surged in the local market as Moslems use a lot of oil for cooking the traditional food items made during the fasting month.

The country's vegoil stocks fell to an estimated 188,000 tonnes last week from 218,000 tonnes a week back, the dealers said. RBD palm oil and palm olein stocks fell to an estimated 160,000 tonnes compared to 180,000 tonnes last week.
Soybean oil and sunflower oil stocks eased to about 16,000 tonnes from 20,000, while the Ghee Corporation of Pakistan's (GCP) palm oil and palm olien stocks fell to 12,000 tonnes from 18,000 tonnes.

One ship with about 6,000 tonnes of soybean oil was expected to arrive at Karachi Port from South America this week. One ship was loading about 25,000 tonnes of palmoil for Pakistan at a Malaysian port while another would load vegoil for Pakistan later this month.
